standard_prerequisites.name: The pushforward of a power of the first Chern class of the twisting sheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, label lemma-cap-projective-bundle, invoked at proof line 6960
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that pushing forward c_1(O_P(1))^s cap pi^*alpha along the bundle is zero for s below r - 1 and returns alpha for s equal to r - 1, which is exactly the injectivity computation. The lemma is claimed separately as S14-algebra-cap-projective-bundle.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flat pullback versus proper pushforward and the projection formula for capping with a first Chern class
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-flat-pullback-proper-pushforward (proof line 6992) and lemma-pushforward-cap-c1 (proof line 6994)
standard_prerequisites.use: Let the surjectivity statement be checked component by component over the disjoint union of the irreducible components of the base, and lets the capping operation be moved through the flat base change.

standard_prerequisites.name: Restriction to an open and the surjectivity of pullback along a morphism with affine space fibres
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, labels lemma-restrict-to-open (proof line 7016), lemma-pullback-affine-fibres-surjective (proof lines 7043 and 7048) and lemma-relative-effective-cartier (proof line 7052)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first two let the base be replaced by a nonempty open and supply the successive lifts from the strata of the projective space, and the third identifies the class of the closure of a stratum with the cap of the first Chern class against the pulled back class.

core_obligations: Prove injectivity: push a relation pi^*alpha_0 + c_1(O_P(1)) cap pi^*alpha_1 + ... + c_1(O_P(1))^{r-1} cap pi^*alpha_{r-1} = 0 forward along pi; the pushforward of a power of the first Chern class vanishes below the top power and returns the class in the top power, so alpha_{r-1} = 0, then cap with c_1(O_P(1)) and repeat to get alpha_{r-2} = 0 and so on (proof lines 6956-6976).

Reduce surjectivity to an irreducible base: with the irreducible components X_i of X and the corresponding P_i, consider the base change square from the disjoint union of the P_i to P over the disjoint union of the X_i, note the pushforward along p is surjective, use flat pullback versus proper pushforward and the projection formula to see that surjectivity for each of the morphisms P_i -> X_i implies surjectivity for pi, and then assume X irreducible so that the dimension is finite and induction on it is available (proof lines 6978-6999).

Reduce to a trivial bundle: after a triviality on a nonempty open the situation is clear when the dimension of X is below k; for general alpha one writes its restriction to the preimage of a nonempty open as gamma_U of a tuple, lifts the components to X, and uses restriction to an open to see that the difference is rationally equivalent to a cycle on the projective bundle over the complement Y of the open, which has smaller dimension, so the induction hypothesis applies and the base may be replaced by any nonempty open; hence one may assume E is free and P is the product of X with a projective space (proof lines 7001-7026).

Finish with the stratification: stratify the projective space into affine spaces whose closures are projective spaces, using that the closure of each stratum represents the corresponding cap of a power of the first Chern class of the twisting sheaf; write alpha restricted to the largest stratum as a pullback, subtract the pullback, use the surjectivity of pullback for affine space fibres to descend the difference successively through the strata, and identify each descended class with the cap of the appropriate power, which produces the required tuple (proof lines 7027-7059).
proof_roadmap: Injectivity by pushing forward the relation and using the top power computation (proof lines 6956-6976).
Surjectivity reduced to an irreducible base through the componentwise base change diagram (proof lines 6978-6999).
Reduction to a trivial bundle by shrinking the base and using induction on its dimension (proof lines 7001-7026).
Conclusion by the affine space stratification of the fibre and the successive descents (proof lines 7027-7059).
difficulty_reason: The theorem is the projective space bundle formula: for a finite locally free sheaf E of rank r on X the map from the direct sum of the Chow groups CH_{k+i}(X), i from 0 to r-1, to CH_{k+r-1}(P) sending a tuple to the sum of the caps of the powers of c_1(O_P(1)) with the pulled back components is an isomorphism (statement lines 6931-6954, tag 02TX). The proof has genuinely different halves: injectivity is a pushforward computation using the fact that the pushforward of the powers of the first Chern class vanishes below the top power, while surjectivity requires reducing to an irreducible base, then to a trivial bundle by shrinking the base with an induction on its dimension, and finally descending a class through the affine space stratification of the projective space stratum by stratum. The stratification descent is the substance, so the claim is H2.
